definitions.title: Vector and Parametric Equations of a Line
definitions.latex: \mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{r}_0 + t\mathbf{v}, \quad x = x_0 + a t, \; y = y_0 + b t, \; z = z_0 + c t
definitions.statement: A line L in space passing through point P_0(x_0, y_0, z_0) parallel to direction vector v = <a, b, c> is parametrized by real t in (-oo, oo). If a, b, c are non-zero, symmetric equations are (x-x_0)/a = (y-y_0)/b = (z-z_0)/c.
definitions.explanation: Extends 2D linear slope to 3D direction vectors without requiring an undefined single slope value.
definitions.keyTakeaway: A line in 3-space requires a point and a direction vector.

definitions.title: Standard Equation of a Plane
definitions.latex: A(x - x_0) + B(y - y_0) + C(z - z_0) = 0 \implies Ax + By + Cz = D
definitions.statement: The plane containing point P_0(x_0, y_0, z_0) with non-zero normal vector n = <A, B, C> consists of all points P(x, y, z) such that the displacement vector P_0 P is orthogonal to n: n . P_0 P = 0.
definitions.explanation: A single linear equation in three variables always defines a plane in Euclidean 3-space.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Coefficients A, B, C in the linear equation directly specify an orthogonal normal vector.
